resource.title: Sakura Bloom 20 mg film-coated tablets - Summary of Product Characteristics

text.div: Synthetic example. Sakura Bloom and Sakuramil are fictitious. This text was written for a FHIR ePI demonstration and must not be used for any clinical purpose.
Sakura Bloom 20 mg film-coated tablets

Each film-coated tablet contains 20 mg Sakuramil.

Excipient with known effect

Each film-coated tablet contains 136 mg lactose (as monohydrate).

For the full list of excipients, see section 6.1.

Film-coated tablet.

Pale red, round, biconvex film-coated tablet, debossed with SB on one side and 20 on the other, approximately 8 mm in diameter.
Clinical particulars.

Sakura Bloom is indicated in adults as an adjunct to diet for the reduction of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in primary hypercholesterolaemia, when the response to diet and other non-pharmacological measures is inadequate.

Posology

Adults

The recommended starting dose is 20 mg once daily. Depending on the LDL-C response, the dose may be increased to 40 mg once daily after at least 4 weeks of treatment. The maximum daily dose is 40 mg.

Older people

No dose adjustment is needed.

Renal impairment

No dose adjustment is needed in mild or moderate renal impairment. In severe renal impairment (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m²) the dose must not exceed 20 mg once daily.

Hepatic impairment

Sakura Bloom is contraindicated in patients with active liver disease (see section 4.3).

Concomitant moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors

In patients taking diltiazem or verapamil the dose must not exceed 20 mg once daily (see section 4.5).

Paediatric population

The safety and efficacy of Sakura Bloom in children and adolescents under 18 years of age have not been established. No data are available.

Method of administration

Oral use. The tablet should be swallowed whole with water, with or without food, at about the same time each day.

• Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.
  • Active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases.
  • Concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole, itraconazole or clarithromycin (see section 4.5).
  • Pregnancy and breast-feeding (see section 4.6).

section.title: 4.4 Special warnings and precautions for use

coding.display: 4.4 Special warnings and precautions for use

code.text: 4.4 Special warnings and precautions for use

text.div:
Liver effects

Liver function tests should be performed before treatment starts, 12 weeks later and periodically thereafter. Treatment should be stopped if transaminases rise persistently above 3 times the upper limit of normal.

Blood pressure

Small increases in blood pressure were observed in clinical studies. Blood pressure should be checked before treatment and at each follow-up visit, particularly in patients with hypertension.

Excipients

Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicinal product.

This medicinal product contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per tablet, that is to say essentially sodium-free.

section.title: 4.5 Interaction with other medicinal products and other forms of interaction

coding.display: 4.5 Interaction with other medicinal products and other forms of interaction

code.text: 4.5 Interaction with other medicinal products and other forms of interaction

text.div:
Sakuramil is metabolised mainly by cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4).

Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors

Ketoconazole increased Sakuramil exposure (AUC) about 4-fold. Use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated (see section 4.3).

Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors

Diltiazem and verapamil increased Sakuramil exposure about 2-fold. The dose must not exceed 20 mg once daily.

CYP3A4 inducers

Rifampicin reduced Sakuramil exposure by about 70%. Concomitant use should be avoided.

Grapefruit juice

Large quantities of grapefruit juice (more than 1 litre a day) should be avoided.

Warfarin

A small increase in INR was seen with warfarin. INR should be monitored when Sakura Bloom is started, stopped or its dose changed.

Pregnancy

There are no data from the use of Sakuramil in pregnant women. Animal studies have shown reproductive toxicity (see section 5.3). Sakura Bloom is contraindicated during pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during treatment.

Breast-feeding

It is unknown whether Sakuramil is excreted in human milk. Sakura Bloom is contraindicated during breast-feeding.

Fertility

No human data are available. Animal studies did not show effects on fertility.

section.title: 4.7 Effects on ability to drive and use machines

coding.display: 4.7 Effects on ability to drive and use machines

code.text: 4.7 Effects on ability to drive and use machines

text.div: Sakura Bloom has minor influence on the ability to drive and use machines. Dizziness has been reported; patients who experience it should not drive or use machines.

Summary of the safety profile

The most common adverse reactions were headache, nausea and myalgia. In clinical studies 3.1% of patients stopped treatment because of an adverse reaction.

Tabulated list of adverse reactions

Frequencies are defined as very common (≥1/10), common (≥1/100 to <1/10), uncommon (≥1/1,000 to <1/100), rare (≥1/10,000 to <1/1,000) and very rare (<1/10,000).

System organ classFrequencyAdverse reaction
Nervous system disordersCommonHeadache
Nervous system disordersUncommonDizziness
Vascular disordersUncommonHypertension
Gastrointestinal disordersCommonNausea
Skin and subcutaneous tissue disordersRareAngioedema, Rash
Musculoskeletal and connective tissue disordersCommonMyalgia
InvestigationsUncommonAlanine aminotransferase increased

Reporting of suspected adverse reactions

Healthcare professionals are asked to report any suspected adverse reactions via the national reporting system.

There is no specific treatment for overdose. Supportive measures should be taken and liver function monitored. Haemodialysis is not expected to remove Sakuramil because it is highly bound to plasma proteins.
Pharmacological properties.

Pharmacotherapeutic group: lipid modifying agents, other. ATC code: not assigned (fictitious substance).

Mechanism of action

Sakuramil is a fictitious substance created for the ICH M4Q(R2) mock-up. In this example it is described as an orally active agent that lowers LDL-C.

Clinical efficacy

In a fictitious 12-week, placebo-controlled study in 480 adults with primary hypercholesterolaemia, LDL-C fell by 31% with 20 mg and 38% with 40 mg, compared with 3% with placebo.

Absorption

Peak plasma concentrations are reached 2 to 4 hours after an oral dose. Food has no relevant effect.

Distribution

Sakuramil is more than 99% bound to plasma proteins.

Biotransformation

Sakuramil is metabolised mainly by CYP3A4 to inactive metabolites.

Elimination

The terminal half-life is about 30 hours. Elimination is mainly in the faeces.

Renal impairment

Exposure was about 1.6-fold higher in severe renal impairment (see section 4.2).

In fictitious repeat-dose studies, increased liver weight and transaminases were seen at exposures above 10 times the clinical exposure. Embryo-fetal toxicity was observed in rats at maternally toxic doses.
Pharmaceutical particulars.

Tablet core

  • Lactose monohydrate
  • Microcrystalline cellulose
  • Croscarmellose sodium
  • Hydroxypropyl cellulose
  • Magnesium stearate

Film-coating

  • Hypromellose
  • Macrogol 6000
  • Titanium dioxide (E171)
  • Iron oxide red (E172)
Not applicable.

Blister: 3 years.

Bottle: 3 years.
